title: Claude Code Usage Tips: PowerShell Alias and Permission Bypass
excerpt: Set up a quick alias c-d for Claude Code in Windows PowerShell and start with --dangerously-skip-permissions by default to reduce repetitive input and permission confirmations.
content:
## Introduction

Recently I've been using Claude Code as my daily coding assistant, and every time in Windows PowerShell I had to type the full command:

```powershell
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
```

My fingers were getting tired. So I added an alias to PowerShell so I can just press `c-d` to enter Claude Code directly.

## Modifying the PowerShell Profile

The path to PowerShell's configuration file is stored in the `$PROFILE` variable. The easiest way to modify it is to open it with Notepad:

```powershell
notepad $PROFILE
```

If it says the file doesn't exist, create it first:

```powershell
New-Item -Path $PROFILE -Type File -Force
```

Then run:

```powershell
notepad $PROFILE
```

## Adding a Claude Code Alias

Add this to the end of the configuration file:

```powershell
function c-d {
    claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
}
```

Save and close Notepad.

> Claude Code officially supports permission mode configuration, allowing you to manage allow/deny rules through permission settings; `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is a way to directly skip permission confirmation.

## Adding a Codex Alias

Similarly, you can configure an alias for Codex in the same configuration file:

```powershell
function c-c {
    codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
}
```

## Usage

After reopening PowerShell next time, simply type:

```powershell
c-d
```

which is equivalent to:

```powershell
claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
```

Claude Code will launch immediately without repeatedly asking for permissions.

## Tips

- If the changes to `$PROFILE` don't take effect, you can run `. $PROFILE` to reload it, or restart PowerShell.
- Different PowerShell versions (Windows PowerShell 5.x / PowerShell 7+) may have separate `$PROFILE` paths, requiring individual configuration.
- If you want a more semantic name, you can also rename the function to `cca`, `clauded`, etc.
